title: Keep ability estimates finite at the extremes
statement: Use an ability estimate that stays finite for all-right and all-wrong answers without pulling the strongest and weakest students toward the average, and test it on extreme answer patterns.
example: One engine's estimate stayed finite and correctly ordered across about 17,900 simulated sessions, with 0 divergences.
detail: A reading assessment's design rejects plain maximum likelihood, which diverges to ±∞ when every answer is right or every answer is wrong, and a prior-based estimate, which shrinks very high and very low scorers toward the prior mean, though they are the students growth tracking most needs (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/01_PSYCHOMETRIC_DESIGN.md`). It uses maximum likelihood with fences, a published method that adds two fictional items 3.8 logits beyond the easiest and hardest items taken, which the reference test also documents (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md`). Its seventh simulation ran all-correct, all-wrong, alternating and rapid-guessing profiles, all finite, fence-bounded and correctly ordered, with 0 divergences in ~17,900 sessions (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`).
against: For the first 2 items the likelihood is nearly flat, so each session still starts on a prior-based estimate and switches after 3 or more responses (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/01_PSYCHOMETRIC_DESIGN.md`, line 112). The stability evidence is simulated, not from real students.

evidence.quote: Pure MLE diverges to ±∞ for all-correct or all-incorrect response patterns.
students with very high or very low ability are shrunk toward the prior mean
items to prevent this divergence without introducing prior-based bias
The 3.8-logit fence offset is NWEA's documented constant
Sim 7: all-correct / all-wrong / alternating / rapid-guessing profiles all finite, fence-bounded, correctly ordered; 0 divergences in ~17,900 sessions

citations.ref: Maximum likelihood score estimation method with fences for short-length tests and computerized adaptive tests, Applied Psychological Measurement 40(4), 289–301 (2016)
